An LRU (Least Recently Used) cache replacement policy manages limited storage by prioritizing data that has been used most recently. When the cache reaches its capacity and a new item must be added, the LRU policy evicts the least recently accessed item to make space. This approach relies on the temporal locality principle, assuming that recently accessed items are more likely to be accessed again soon.

Commonly, a doubly linked list is used where each item access involves moving it to the front, ensuring the least recently used item is always at the back.
